director.chapterArc: Escalation from shock to tactical acceptance, then physical depletion and isolation.
director.restraintNote: Maintain Callie's analytical voice even during panic; Katori remains flatly factual. Avoid melodrama in the mother/Callie exchange or the horse incident.

cues.delivery: Observational. Calmly establish the threat's direction without alarm.
cues.from: Callie heard it first. It was the grinding sound of loose stone rolling ahead of a weight, twenty feet below the lip of the causeway and a little behind her. It was not coming up toward the wagon or the gap at the wheel, and it was not heading for the long silver pools of ash along the low edge of the deck. It was coming straight up the slope toward the place where she was standing.
cues.through: It did not catch. It didn't even slow down. The hoop was a bent ash-wood rib as thick as her wrist, and the grey edge went through it the way a wire goes through soft cheese. The top half of the hoop sagged into the canvas and hung there, and the whole of the back of the wagon went lopsided in the dark.
cues.reason: Scene setup requires neutral grounding before action.

cues.delivery: Urgent but controlled command. Katori's voice is flat and direct.
cues.from: "Down," said Katori. "Callie. It's on the rock, down."
cues.through: The husk came over the shoulder of the embankment on all four points with its head low. Callie did not swing, because she did not trust anything that swung any more. She stepped across its line the way she had stepped across a hundred of them and put the hook over its back from the outside.
cues.reason: Immediate tactical instruction during combat.

cues.delivery: Detached observation. Describe the supernatural impact as a physical fact.
cues.from: It stopped against her. There was the same flat enormous note she had heard when the horse's hoof struck, only smaller, a mallet on a stump instead of a maul. The husk folded against nothing a finger's width off her coat, and she did not move at all. She simply watched it happen, like a girl looking through a window at weather.
cues.through: It was quiet again. Somewhere up the wagon Duchess was breathing like a bellows.
cues.reason: Callie's internal state is numb; narration must reflect this dissociation.

cues.delivery: Ines speaks with functional clarity. Callie's reply is flat acknowledgment.
cues.from: "It came for you," Ines said. She was standing on the crate stack with the skillet held low against her leg. "Not the wagon. It went past the wheel. It went past me. It came straight for you."
cues.through: "I know," said Callie.
cues.reason: Dialogue serves to confirm the threat target.

cues.delivery: Katori's tone is matter-of-fact revelation. No awe in her voice.
cues.from: "You asked me which one," said Katori. "It's both. That's your answer. I'm sorry it took me as long as it did." She lifted her right hand, the one with the blade in it. "Now watch me, because I'm going to do this once, and then I want you standing with your back to that wagon."
cues.through: Callie could not do it.
cues.reason: Revealing the 'both' status requires factual delivery.

cues.delivery: Callie's internal struggle described with physical precision. Katori agrees without drama.
cues.from: She did not know what she was trying. That was the first problem, and it was a bigger problem than she would have guessed. She tried to let go of the hook in her head, the way you would let go of a rope. She tried to want it shorter. She shut her eyes and tried to feel for the edge of the thing closed over her and push it off like a blanket, and there was no edge to it. It was just on her, everywhere, the way cold is on you.
cues.through: "No," Katori agreed. "I didn't think you could. It was worth one try."
cues.reason: The failure to disengage is a mechanical problem.

cues.delivery: Instructional. Katori guides Callie through the physical test.
cues.from: "I'm thinking." Katori had come the rest of the way down the wagon and stopped a pace off, closer than she had been, and she was looking at Callie the way she had looked at her on the first morning, over the top of the fire, as if she was reading a snare. "Put the hook down on the deck. Don't throw it. Set it down."
cues.through: She picked it up. The pulling stopped.
cues.reason: The experiment requires clear, step-by-step narration.

cues.delivery: Callie's realization of her role as bait. Voice remains analytical.
cues.from: Callie had worked that out a second before Katori said it, and it went through her like cold water.
cues.through: "It's me," she said. "They're coming at me."
cues.reason: The shift from victim to tool is a logical deduction.

cues.delivery: Katori cuts off the suggestion with pragmatic efficiency.
cues.from: "You should go on without me. Take the wagon and go on, and I'll come behind when —"
cues.through: Pell had not let go of the horse.
cues.reason: The interruption is a tactical correction.

cues.delivery: Pell's voice remains flat and steady despite the crisis.
cues.from: He was up at the front with both hands in her cheekpieces, and he was still talking in the same low, flat voice. He had been talking for so long that it had stopped being words and become something more like weather. Duchess stood splay-legged against the pole with her head high and her eyes showing white all the way round. Every few seconds the dead trace on the far side jerked, as the weight at the bottom of it settled in the rocks. Every time it jerked, it pulled the pole a finger's width toward the edge, and every time the pole moved, the horse screamed.
cues.through: Otto went for it. He had his knife out in his good hand, and his other arm was wrapped to the elbow in something that had been Ines's scarf and was now black. He got down on his knees at the front of the wagon and reached in under the pole toward the singletree on the far side, where the trace was hooked. Then he stopped, because the whole thing was bar-tight and humming. Anything that cut it close would take the hand that cut it.
cues.reason: Establishes Pell's stoicism under pressure.

cues.delivery: Callie acts with decisive speed. The action is described mechanically.
cues.from: Callie was already moving.
cues.through: The end of it went down the rock with a hiss, and whatever was at the bottom of it went on being at the bottom. Up at the front, all at once, there was nothing holding Duchess to the edge of the world.
cues.reason: The solution requires precise physical description.

cues.delivery: High tension but physically grounded. The wagon's movement is described as weight and pressure.
cues.from: She went forward. Of course she did. She went the only way that was open to her, a hard plunging lunge against Pell's hands. The pole swung with her. The wagon swung with the pole. The off rear wheel, which had been hung on the rail stub all this time, came up off the stub and dropped, and it did not drop onto the deck. It dropped outboard, over the lip, into air.
cues.through: The wagon came onto her. It came onto her the way the kick had and the way the husks had. She felt none of the weight, only a kind of pressure, the way you feel the wind when you are standing inside a house. She saw the tailboard stop a finger off her coat. She saw the axle stop. The wagon had been going over, and it stopped going over, and it stayed stopped, hanging off its corner at a slant against a thirteen-year-old girl, with her arms not even braced.
cues.reason: The physical feat must feel impossible yet real.

cues.delivery: Katori's voice is barely audible. Callie lies with calm certainty.
cues.from: "Callie," said Katori, very quietly.
cues.through: "Otto," said Katori, in exactly the same voice. "Pole."
cues.reason: The aftermath requires quiet restraint.

cues.delivery: Callie's physical reaction (shaking/cold) described with sensory detail.
cues.from: It took them four minutes, and they were the longest four minutes Callie had ever stood through, because she had nothing at all to do in them except stand.
cues.through: Otto sat down on the road with the pole across his knees and his bad arm held against his chest.
cues.reason: The toll of the power is a physiological fact.

cues.delivery: Otto's apology and Ines's dry comfort. Flat cadence.
cues.from: "Sorry," he said to nobody. "About before. About being sick."
cues.through: "All right," said Otto, and his voice went up at the end, and he put his head down on his knees.
cues.reason: Character interaction is functional.

cues.delivery: Callie's observation of Ines. Quiet realization.
cues.from: Ines stood up and took the lamp off its hook under the board and went off down the causeway with it. She did not explain. Callie watched the light go along the deck at a slow walk, low, swinging left and right. Then she understood. Ines was walking back along the length of the fight, looking for arrows.
cues.through: Callie went to the back of the wagon, where her mother was.
cues.reason: Narrative recovery and setup for the next beat.

cues.delivery: Mother's voice is weary but sharp. Callie's reaction is numb.
cues.from: "Well," said her mother. "That's new."
cues.through: That was the kind of thing her mother said, and it was the kind of thing she would say whether it was true or not. Callie went anyway.
cues.reason: The emotional core lies in the mother's quiet validation.

cues.delivery: Ines and Katori exchange data. Callie makes the tactical call.
cues.from: Ines came back with four arrows.
cues.through: "No," said Katori. "It isn't. Callie. The back."
cues.reason: The decision to leave ash is a logical calculation.

cues.delivery: Pell's explanation of the horse's fear. Callie accepts her isolation.
cues.from: They could not put Duchess anywhere near her.
cues.through: "You'll stay back there," Pell agreed. "And I'll thank you to stay back there all the way over, and not come up, whatever you hear."
cues.reason: The separation is a tactical necessity.

cues.delivery: Callie's isolation and physical decline. Katori's observation is clinical.
cues.from: They came at her the whole way.
cues.through: The lamp stayed where it was for a moment. Then Katori came back down the road with it. She did not come the whole way. She stopped five or six paces off and held the lamp up and looked at Callie's face, and whatever she saw there, her own face did not change.
cues.reason: The depletion must feel slow and inevitable.

cues.delivery: Katori's diagnosis of the cost. Pell's final warning is flat.
cues.from: "How cold?" she said.
cues.through: "The span," said Pell. "We're at the span. And she won't put a foot on it."
cues.reason: The chapter ends on a factual threat.

pauses.after: "No," she said again, and she heard her grandfather in it and did not mind. "Ash calls them to where it is. It calls them here, to this bit of road, and it doesn't care whether we're standing on it. If we lift it, we're here for an hour, on our knees, with a lamp, while it calls, and while I call. If we leave it, it keeps calling here, and we're somewhere else." She swallowed. "Leave it. Come back for it in the light."
pauses.reason: Completed thought on the ash strategy.
